units.zh: 卓行 ○蕭劄剌耶律官奴蕭蒲離不
units.en: Outstanding Conduct ○ Xiao Zhalaci, Yelü Guannu, Xiao Pulibu
units.literal: Outstanding Conduct ○ Xiao Zhalaci, Yelü Guannu, Xiao Pulibu

units.zh: 遼之共國任事，耶律、蕭二族而已。
units.en: In running the Liao state, only the Yelü and Xiao clans held office.
units.literal: In jointly governing the Liao state and serving in affairs, only the Yelü and Xiao two clans were employed.

units.zh: 二族之中，有退然自足，不淫於富貴，不詘於聲利，可以振頹風，激薄俗，亦足嘉尚者，得三人焉。
units.en: Within those two clans there were men who held themselves apart in quiet contentment, untouched by wealth and rank, unbowed before fame and profit, able to revive a failing moral climate and rouse a jaded age — men truly worth honoring. Three such men were found.
units.literal: Among the two clans were those who withdrew with self-sufficiency, were not dissolute amid wealth and rank, were not bent by fame and gain, could rouse a declining ethos and stir a shallow custom — also worthy of praise — three men were found.

units.zh: 作《卓行傳》。
units.en: The "Biographies of Outstanding Conduct" was compiled.
units.literal: Composed the "Biographies of Outstanding Conduct."

units.zh: 蕭劄剌，字虛輦，北府宰相排押之弟。
units.en: Xiao Zhalaci, whose style was Xunian, was the younger brother of Paiya, Chancellor of the Northern Administration.
units.literal: Xiao Zhalaci, style name Xunian, younger brother of the Chancellor of the Northern Administration Paiya.

units.zh: 性介特，不事生業。
units.en: By nature he was reserved and unconventional, and he took no interest in making a living.
units.literal: By nature aloof and unusual, he did not engage in livelihood pursuits.

units.zh: 保寧間，以戚屬進，累遷寧遠軍節度使。
units.en: During the Baoning era he entered office through imperial kinship and rose in stages to Military Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army.
units.literal: During Baoning, through imperial kinship he entered service and was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army.

units.zh: 秩滿裏居，淡泊自適。
units.en: When his term expired he went home to live in the countryside, content in plain simplicity.
units.literal: When his term ended he returned home to live, plain and self-contented.

units.zh: 統和末，召為南京馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: Near the end of the Tonghe reign he was summoned to serve as Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry at the Southern Capital.
units.literal: At the end of Tonghe, he was summoned as Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry at the Southern Capital.

units.zh: 以疾求退，不聽，遷夷離畢。
units.en: He asked to resign on grounds of illness, but the request was denied; instead he was transferred to the post of Yilijibi.
units.literal: He asked to retire on grounds of illness; this was not granted, and he was transferred to Yilijibi.

units.zh: 又以疾辭，許之。
units.en: He declined once more, again citing illness, and this time permission was granted.
units.literal: Again he declined on account of illness, and this was permitted.

units.zh: 遂入頡山，杜門不出。
units.en: He then withdrew to Jie Mountain and shut his door, never going out.
units.literal: He thereupon entered Jie Mountain and shut his door, not going out.

units.zh: 上嘉其志，不復征，劄剌自是家於頡山。
units.en: The emperor admired his resolve and summoned him no more; from that time Zhalaci made his home on Jie Mountain.
units.literal: The emperor commended his resolve and no longer summoned him; from then on Zhalaci made his home on Jie Mountain.

units.zh: 親友或過之，終日言不及世務。
units.en: When relatives and friends came to see him, he would talk all day without once touching on worldly affairs.
units.literal: When kin and friends sometimes visited him, all day he spoke of nothing touching worldly affairs.

units.zh: 凡宴遊相邀，亦不拒。
units.en: When invited to feasts or outings he did not refuse.
units.literal: Whenever feasts and outings invited him, he did not refuse either.

units.zh: 一歲山居過半，與世俗不偶。
units.en: He spent more than half of each year in the mountains and kept aloof from ordinary society.
units.literal: More than half the year he dwelt in the mountains, uncongenial with the worldly.

units.zh: 耶律資忠重之，目曰頡山老人。
units.en: Yelü Zizhong held him in high regard and called him the Old Man of Jie Mountain.
units.literal: Yelü Zizhong esteemed him and called him the Old Man of Jie Mountain.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 耶律官奴，字奚隱，林牙斡魯之孫。
units.en: Yelü Guannu, whose style was Xiyin, was the grandson of Linya Wolu.
units.literal: Yelü Guannu, style name Xiyin, grandson of Linya Wolu.

units.zh: 沈厚多學，詳於本朝世系。
units.en: Steady and learned, he was thoroughly versed in the genealogy of his own dynasty.
units.literal: Deep and substantial, widely learned, well versed in the current dynasty's genealogy.

units.zh: 嗜酒好佚。
units.en: He loved wine and took his ease.
units.literal: He loved wine and delighted in ease.

units.zh: 初，徵為宿直將軍。
units.en: At first he was summoned to serve as Night-Watch Duty General.
units.literal: At first he was summoned as Duty General on Night Watch.

units.zh: 重熙九年，以疾去官。
units.en: In the ninth year of Chongxi he left office on grounds of illness.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Chongxi, he left office on account of illness.

units.zh: 上以官奴屬尊，欲成其志，乃許自擇一路節度使。
units.en: Because Guannu was of distinguished lineage, the emperor wished to satisfy his wishes and allowed him to choose for himself any circuit military commissionership.
units.literal: The emperor, considering Guannu senior in lineage, wished to fulfill his wish and permitted him to choose for himself a circuit military commissioner.

units.zh: 官奴辭曰：「臣愚鈍，不任官使。」
units.en: Guannu declined, saying, "Your servant is dull and incompetent, unfit for official duty."
units.literal: Guannu declined, saying: "Your servant is dull-witted and cannot bear official commissions."

units.zh: 加歸義軍節度使，輒請致政。
units.en: He was nevertheless appointed Military Commissioner of the Guiyi Army, but immediately asked to retire from office.
units.literal: He was added as Military Commissioner of the Guiyi Army but at once requested retirement from office.

units.zh: 官奴與歐裏部人蕭哇友善，哇謂官奴曰：「仕不能致主澤民，成大功烈，何屑屑為也！
units.en: Guannu was on friendly terms with Xiao Wa of the Ouli tribe. Wa said to Guannu, "If in office one cannot bring benefit to one's lord and grace to the people, or achieve great deeds, why bother with such trifles!
units.literal: Guannu was friendly with Xiao Wa of the Ouli tribe; Wa said to Guannu: "In service one cannot shower the ruler with benefit and the people with grace, or achieve great merit — why fuss over such things!

units.zh: 吾與若居林下，以枕簟自隨，觴詠自樂，雖不官，無慊焉。」
units.en: You and I can live in the woods, carry our pillows and mats with us, and find our pleasure in wine and verse — and though we hold no office, we shall want for nothing."
units.literal: You and I shall dwell in the groves, take pillow and mat with us, toast and verse for our own pleasure — though without office, we shall lack nothing."

units.zh: 官奴然之。
units.en: Guannu agreed.
units.literal: Guannu agreed with this.

units.zh: 時稱「二逸」。
units.en: People of the time called them the "Two Recluses."
units.literal: They were called at the time the "Two Recluses."

units.zh: 乾統間，官奴卒。
units.en: During the Qiantong era Guannu died.
units.literal: During Qiantong, Guannu died.

units.zh: 蕭蒲離不，字桵懶，魏國王惠之四世孫。
units.en: Xiao Pulibu, whose style was Suilan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Wei.
units.literal: Xiao Pulibu, style name Suilan, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Wei.

units.zh: 父母蚤喪，鞠於祖父兀古匿。
units.en: His parents died while he was young, and he was raised by his grandfather Wuguni.
units.literal: His parents died early; he was reared by his grandfather Wuguni.

units.zh: 性孝悌。
units.en: By nature he was filial and dutiful toward his kin.
units.literal: By nature filial and fraternal.

units.zh: 年十三，兀古匿卒，自以早失怙恃，復遭祖喪，哀毀逾禮，族裏嘉嘆。
units.en: At thirteen, when Wuguni died, he felt that he had already lost his parents early and now faced his grandfather's death as well; his mourning exceeded the prescribed rites, and his kinsmen praised and marveled at it.
units.literal: At age thirteen Wuguni died; he himself had early lost his parents and again met his grandfather's bereavement; his grief exceeded the rites, and the clan praised and sighed at it.

units.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「我於親不得終養，今誰為訓者？
units.en: He once said to others, "I was unable to care for my parents to the end — who is left to guide me now?
units.literal: He once said to others: "I could not tend my kin to the end — who now is there to instruct me?

units.zh: 茍不自勉，何以報鞠育恩！」
units.en: If I do not strive on my own, how can I repay the kindness of being raised!"
units.literal: If I do not urge myself on, how can I repay the grace of nurturing!"

units.zh: 自是力學，於文藝無不精。
units.en: From then on he studied hard, and there was no branch of letters and arts in which he did not excel.
units.literal: From then on he studied with effort and in literary arts there was nothing he did not master.

units.zh: 乾統間，以兀古匿之故召之，不應。
units.en: During the Qiantong era he was summoned on account of Wuguni's standing, but he did not answer the call.
units.literal: During Qiantong, on account of Wuguni he was summoned; he did not respond.

units.zh: 常與親識遊獵山水，奉養無長物仆隸，欣欣如也。
units.en: He often roamed the hills and waters hunting with relatives and friends; he lived simply, without fine possessions or a large retinue of servants, yet he was always content.
units.literal: He often roamed mountains and waters hunting with kin and acquaintances; in supporting himself he had no lavish goods or many servants, yet was cheerful indeed.

units.zh: 或曰：「公胡不念以嗣先世功名？」
units.en: Someone asked him, "Sir, why do you not consider carrying on your ancestors' fame and achievements?"
units.literal: Someone said: "Sir, why do you not think to carry on your forebears' fame and merit?"

units.zh: 答曰：「自度不足以繼先業，年逾強仕，安能益主庇民！」
units.en: He replied, "I judge myself unfit to continue the family legacy; my years are already past the prime of service — how could I bring benefit to the ruler or shelter the people!"
units.literal: He answered: "I estimate myself insufficient to continue the ancestors' work; my years have passed the prime of service — how could I benefit the ruler and shelter the people!"

units.zh: 累征，皆以疾辭。
units.en: He was summoned repeatedly, and each time declined on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Repeated summons — on all he declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 晚年，謝絕人事，卜居抹古山，屏遠葷茹，潛心佛書，延有道者談論彌日。
units.en: In his later years he withdrew from worldly affairs, chose a home on Mogu Mountain, abstained from meat and strong flavors, devoted himself to Buddhist texts, and would invite men of insight to talk with him from morning till night.
units.literal: In his later years he declined human affairs, chose residence on Mogu Mountain, kept far from meat and pungent foods, devoted his mind to Buddhist books, and invited men of the Way to discuss all day.

units.zh: 人問所得何如，但曰：「有深樂！
units.en: When people asked what he had gained from this, he would only say, "There is deep joy!
units.literal: When people asked what he had gained, he only said: "There is deep joy!

units.zh: 惟覺六鑿不相攘，餘無知者。」
units.en: I only feel that the six openings no longer contend with one another — beyond that I know nothing."
units.literal: Only I feel the six borers do not struggle against one another — beyond that I have no knowledge."

units.zh: 一日，易服，無疾而逝。
units.en: One day he changed his clothes and passed away without any sign of illness.
units.literal: One day he changed his clothes and passed away without illness.

units.zh: 論曰：隱固未易為也，而亦未可輕以與人。
units.en: The historian remarks: True reclusion is not easily achieved, nor should the name be lightly bestowed on anyone.
units.literal: Discussion says: Reclusion is indeed not easily achieved, and likewise it cannot lightly be granted to others.

units.zh: 若劄剌謝職不談時務，官奴兩辭節鎮，蒲離不召而不赴，雖未足謂之隱，然在當時能知內外之分，甘於肥遁，不猶愈於求富貴利達而為妻妾羞者哉？
units.en: Zhalaci resigned his post and would not discuss current affairs; Guannu twice declined regional commands; Pulibu was summoned but did not go — though these do not fully qualify as reclusion, in their own day they knew the boundary between public duty and private life and were content to withdraw from the world. Are they not still preferable to those who scrambled for wealth, rank, and advancement and brought shame upon their households?
units.literal: As for Zhalaci resigning office and not discussing current affairs, Guannu twice declining circuit commands, Pulibu summoned yet not attending — though not quite enough to be called recluses, yet in that time able to know the division of inner and outer, content in ample withdrawal — are they not still better than those who sought wealth, rank, and advancement and brought shame upon their wives and concubines?

units.zh: 故稱卓行可也。
units.en: It is fitting, then, to call their conduct outstanding.
units.literal: Hence calling them outstanding conduct is fitting.

units.zh: 六月辛酉朔，遣中丞耶律資忠使高麗，取六州舊地。
units.en: On the xinyou new moon of the sixth month Censor Yelü Zizhong was sent as envoy to Goryeo to recover the six old prefectures.
units.literal: Sixth month, on the xinyou new moon, Censor Yelü Zizhong was dispatched as envoy to Goryeo to recover the six old prefectures.

units.zh: 北府宰相排押。
units.en: Paiya, Northern Chancellor.
units.literal: Northern Chancellor Paiya.

units.zh: 兀古匿。
units.en: Wuguni.
units.literal: Wuguni.

units.zh: 蒲離不。

instructions: Review every case and every target local person. Quote the primary Chinese for each target and the retained canonical anchor. Confirm actual individual, supported chapter attribution, and accepted membership; hold contradictions. Keep unresolvedIdentity true when proposed, including small candidate buckets and overflow.
